findings.title: Rejected devices are cached and allowed on retry
findings.body: tagDeviceUI inserts the device into the 29-minute local cache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and does not evict the entry when that call fails. A new device rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached therefore fails authentication once, but its next request hits the cache, TagDevice returns nil, and Anonymous.Authenticate issues an identity even though the device was never stored or counted. The device limit can be bypassed simply by retrying the same device ID.

findings.title: Device-limit check is not atomic with device insertion
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice performs CountDevices in one DB session and the subsequent insert/upsert in another, without a transaction, lock, or atomic conditional insert. Concurrent requests, including requests handled by different Grafana instances sharing the database, can all observe a count below the limit and insert distinct devices, causing the configured limit to be exceeded.

findings.title: Omitting the device ID bypasses the device limit
findings.body: TagDevice returns nil when the X-Grafana-Device-Id header is absent, after which Anonymous.Authenticate still returns an anonymous identity. Any non-browser client, or a client that strips this voluntary header, can therefore use anonymous access without being counted or subjected to AnonymousDeviceLimit, undermining the limit as an access control.

findings.title: Provider signature changes are not reflected in dependency-injection wiring
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now requires db.DB instead of anonstore.AnonStore, while ProvideAnonDBStore now additionally requires a bare int64 that Wire cannot construct. The PR contains no regenerated wire_gen.go or wire-set update, so the existing generated injector that supplies the old arguments will no longer compile and Wire generation for the anonymous store provider cannot resolve int64.

findings.title: Limit tests do not cover allowed existing devices or the authentication path
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks sequentially that a second distinct device is rejected by the store. It does not verify that an already-counted device can still be updated when the count equals the limit, nor does it exercise AnonDeviceService.TagDevice or Anonymous.Authenticate with a non-zero configured limit (the service tests use a default cfg with limit 0), leaving the main enforcement and retry behavior untested.

findings.title: New device_limit setting is not documented or added to sample configuration
findings.body: The PR parses auth.anonymous device_limit but adds no entry to conf/defaults.ini or conf/sample.ini and no documentation update. Operators have no discoverable documentation for the new option, its units/scope (devices seen in the last 30 days), or that 0 means unlimited.
